final.executive_summary: Underweight AAPL: execute the partial trim to a 0.5% target weight at the next session open (execution_action=rebalance, target_weight_now=0.005), selling roughly 1.6 of the 3.21 shares held for about $498 of notional protected against a ~$0.50 fee, and do not anchor to the $314.85 average cost. I explicitly reject the conservative desk's zero target — with total equity of ~$99,608 and 99% of it in cash, a 1.01% stub is already a cheap option and liquidating it to dodge an unmodelable next-open event is not risk management, it is churn. I equally reject the aggressive desk's 2.5–3% reload as written, because its own trigger geometry is sub-1:1. Narrative conditions, not implemented orders: cut the remainder on two consecutive closes below 308.80; treat a close below 300.00 as a full-exit signal; consider re-risking only on a daily close above 320.28 on >55M shares (ideally on the neutral's 315–316 retest with a 311.00 stop, which is the version that actually clears 1.5:1) or on Q4 FY26 gross margin at/above 50% with memory cost quantified and hedge coverage disclosed.
final.investment_thesis:
The decision is Underweight rather than Sell because the direction question is genuinely undecidable on this packet while the entry question is decidable, and it resolves against holding full size at $313.45.

What decided it — the forward risk/reward, not the trailing record. The franchise evidence is not seriously contested: nine-month revenue +16.1%, Q3 gross margin 50.06%, diluted EPS +22.4%, normalized FCF +37.5%, $62.2B net cash, and a real 2nm roadmap. The aggressive desk's operating-leverage point is also correct on its own terms — Q3 cost of goods and services +8.6% against revenue +16.4%, with gross profit growth accelerating three straight quarters — and the inventory bear argument is weaker than advertised, since finished goods fell (3,447 vs 3,594) while raw materials rose 260%, which reads more like ramp pre-positioning than demand failure. That is why this is not Sell and why the conservative desk's 0.000 target is the wrong instrument: he invoked a 2.5–3% reload as a 'fivefold increase' when three sizes of that stub risk roughly 0.14% of equity in a 99%-cash book. Rhetoric, not calibration.

But the bear wins the price. The mechanical point is decisive and unanswered: nine-month opex grew +21.9% against revenue +16.1%, so operating margin expanded only because gross margin expanded faster. If gross margin flattens while R&D compounds, operating leverage inverts — and the conservative is right that the 50.06% June print predates the August memory-cost reporting (AI-server pricing up >15%), which makes it the last clean number before the variable changed, not proof of durability. The aggressive desk's counter that the memory squeeze is 'inference without magnitude' cuts both ways: absent quantification is a reason to be cautious, not comfortable. Add the reversal of the $10.8B cash-tax benefit (cash OCF growth is ~+29.9%, not +43.1%), the $13.3B gross intangible with no matching acquisition outflow against a +$13.5B rise in other noncurrent liabilities, the 28% capex decline flattering FCF, and buybacks down 12% YoY while cash sits at a record — a capital-allocation shift the neutral correctly labels inference rather than disclosure, but still not a bid.

On the tape, the neutral's correction to the conservative must be accepted: the claim that 'down days carried heavier volume' is incomplete — 8/19 was +2.19% on 50.5M shares, heavier than the 41.0M and 46.9M down days that followed. Volume is genuinely ambiguous. But the pattern that survives is the one that matters for entry: the pre-leaked Mac refresh moved the stock only +1.15% on 34.0M shares, 68% of average and the second lightest session of the month; the 8/20 rejection at 320.28 is unbroken; the 7/31 gap (310.69–329.59) remains unfilled after eighteen sessions; and price sits only 0.72% above the 50-SMA at 311.22, which is confirmation with zero margin of safety. The 'triple confluence' at 309.11–311.22 is three correlated moving averages, not three independent buyers.

The asymmetry arithmetic is where both bullish expressions fail. At $313.45 with a statistically valid 2xATR (14.4-point) stop, reward to the first target at 327.74 is ~13.3 points against 14.4 of risk — under 1:1 — so adding at spot is not justified. The aggressive desk's own reload at 320.30 with the same 14.4-point stop is 7.46 points of reward against 14.4 of risk (0.52:1), or 0.91:1 to the 333.43 gap fill, and sizing that at 2.5–3% is not 'paying for confirmation,' it is paying up for the worst entry on the board. The neutral found the real fix: a stop at 311.00 under the 50-SMA is structural rather than mechanical, and turns the reload into ~1.4:1 on the same entry. That is a condition to consider later, not a position to hold now. The trader's alternative patient entry — the 310.26–311.22 retest with a stop under 306 — is the ~1.9:1 trade, and it costs nothing to wait for because there is no obligation to be long.

Why not Hold. A Hold here would keep 1.01% at a price where the aggressive desk's own numbers cannot clear 2:1, and would treat 'the evidence is balanced' as a reason to do nothing when the position-level math points down. Why not Overweight. The 8/17 Underweight (+2.7% alpha) and 8/13 Underweight (+3.9% alpha) cost real alpha by trimming momentum decay inside a live golden cross with price ~11% above a rising 200-SMA — that lesson binds, and it is exactly why the trim is to 0.5% and not to zero, and why the remainder keeps optionality on a squeeze resolution out of the 8.46% band. Why not Sell. The conservative's zero target requires conviction in a downside resolution the evidence cannot support, and it maximizes trades: liquidate, then re-enter at 320.28, is two more trades than one. The neutral's sizing argument wins the execution question outright — zero is sized to conviction nobody has, 2.5–3% is sized to a breakout that hasn't happened, and 0.5% is sized to 'I don't know, so keep the option cheap.'

The 0.5% trim is also honestly trivial in dollars: ~$498 of notional, ~$0.50 in fees against the $46.80 already burned. Its value is not the alpha on the stub; it is refusing to keep capital deployed at an entry whose own bull trigger pays less than one unit of reward per unit of risk, and stopping the daily target-chasing that generated the fee tally in the first place. Hold the stub with keep_shares between sessions rather than rebalancing to a drifting target.

What would change it. Upgrade toward Overweight on a daily close above 320.28 on >55M shares that holds the gap floor, ideally entered as a 315–316 retest with a 311.00 stop (~1.4:1); or on Q4 FY26 gross margin at/above 50% with memory cost explicitly quantified and hedge coverage disclosed. Downgrade toward Sell on FQ4 gross margin below 48% with revenue growth decelerating, on the $13.3B inventory build failing to unwind, or on a close below 300.00 that is not reclaimed. Gaps stated, not papered over: the ~32x forward earnings and ~3% FCF yield are the research desk's assertions and there is no consensus series or independent multiple cross-check in the packet; no options chain or implied-vol data, so no hedge or collar can be priced against the Nvidia print and inflation number landing on the decision date; no segment or geographic margin attribution, so 50.06% durability is unattributable; the $13.3B intangible and +$13.5B other noncurrent liability carry no footnote; and the cause of the 7/31 gap remains unestablished, so 310.69–329.59 is carried as unquantified event risk. Every level here is technical, not valuation-derived, and the next-open execution price is unknown.
final.time_horizon: 1-3 months, re-underwritten at the late-October FQ4 FY26 print
